title: Stonebridge photo upload postmortem
brief: Please write up the postmortem for INC-3017 at Stonebridge Realty, the listing photo upload outage on 2026-08-27, owned by the Listings Platform team. The numbers people will ask about first: it lasted 112 minutes, upload failures peaked at 100 percent, 8340 listings were left with missing photos, and 412 support tickets came in. What happened, for a "Summary" section: a storage policy change meant to restrict bucket access to our VPC endpoint also blocked uploads made with pre-signed URLs from agents' phones, so every mobile upload returned 403. Then "Timeline" with times in UTC, annotate the moments that mattered: 10:15 policy change applied through Terraform; 10:22 uploads begin failing with 403; 10:31 first customer ticket reaches support; 10:48 incident declared Sev2; 11:20 the policy diff is identified as the cause; 11:58 hotfix applied removing the deny statement; 12:07 uploads recover. A "Why it was not caught" section covering: the change was tested only from the office network, staging has no mobile upload test, and the policy linter does not model pre-signed URLs. A "What went well" section: the declared incident had a clear commander within 17 minutes, and the rollback itself took under 10 minutes once the cause was known. Finish with "Action items", each with an owner and due date: add a pre-signed URL upload test to staging, Greta Lindqvist, 2026-09-18; require policy changes to be applied to staging first, Omar Haddad, 2026-09-25; alert when upload 403s exceed 2 percent for 5 minutes, Listings on-call, 2026-09-11. Blameless tone.

edit.request: Add an action item "Run a game day for storage policy changes", owner Yuki Tanabe, due 2026-10-30, and correct the support ticket count to 436.
